subject.title: [Feature]: Memory durability config — hard flush threshold, priority-aware compaction, cache TTL

question: Should OpenClaw add public config/runtime contracts for hard token-based memory flush, priority-preserving compaction metadata, and embedding-cache TTL, and should those land as one bundle or as separate decisions?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the request defines new public memory/config semantics in an area where repository policy sets a high bar for config surface, durability behavior, and plugin/runtime ownership.

options.title: Split Contract Decisions
options.body: Approve or reject hard flush, priority preservation, and cache TTL separately so each gets focused schema, docs, tests, and rollout decisions.

options.title: Accept The Bundle
options.body: Treat the three knobs as one memory durability feature and require a broader design/implementation PR covering all schema and runtime surfaces together.

options.title: Defer New Config Surface
options.body: Keep current soft flush, safeguard compaction, and content-hash cache behavior, and ask for narrower failure evidence before adding more public knobs.

recommendation.title: Split Contract Decisions
recommendation.body: Approve or reject hard flush, priority preservation, and cache TTL separately so each gets focused schema, docs, tests, and rollout decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current and historical signals for memory flush, compaction config, and embedding-cache ownership point to steipete.
